t.3.67.1: Mother, if you wish me to stay alive, I tell you the truth: strive to bring back that hero among men, Nala.
t.3.67.3: Then, seeing her in that condition, the whole inner palace was filled with exceeding cries of 'Alas, alas!' and wept bitterly.
t.3.67.2: Thus addressed by Damayantī, the queen, deeply grieved and choked with tears, O king, said nothing at all in reply.
t.3.67.4: Then, great king, his wife spoke these words to Bhīma: “Damayantī, your daughter, grieves for her husband.”
t.3.67.5: And casting aside her shame, O king, she herself said to me: “Let your servants strive to find Puṇyaśloka.”
t.3.67.6: Urged by her, the king dispatched obedient brāhmaṇas in all directions, saying, "Strive to find Nala."
t.3.67.7: Then, at the command of the lord of Vidarbha, those bulls among brāhmaṇas went to see Damayantī and said to her, "We are setting out."
t.3.67.8: Then Bhaimī said to them: "In all the kingdoms, in the assemblies of the people, speak these words, here and there, again and again."
t.3.67.9: Where have you gone, O gambler, having cut away half of my garment, abandoning me, your loving and devoted beloved, asleep in the forest, O beloved?
t.3.67.10: Just as she was instructed, she waits there, watching for you, the young woman burning intensely with grief, wrapped in half a garment.
t.3.67.12: This and something more should be said, so that he may show compassion toward me: for fire, when fanned by the wind, burns down the forest.
t.3.67.11: O king, show favor to her who weeps constantly with that grief; be gracious, O hero, and give her a reply.
t.3.67.13: A wife must always be supported and protected by her husband. Why then have both these duties perished in you, though you are one who knows dharma?
t.3.67.14: You were always renowned as wise, nobly born and compassionate; yet you have become pitiless, I suspect because my good fortune has run out.
t.3.67.15: So show compassion to me, great archer, bull among men; for non-cruelty is the highest dharma, and this I have heard from you yourself.
t.3.67.16: If anyone should reply to you as you speak thus, that man must by all means be found out: who he is and where he dwells.
t.3.67.17: And whatever reply a man may give on hearing your words, take up that speech and report it to me quickly, O best of the twice-born.
t.3.67.18: You must act tirelessly so that he does not know that you are wandering about at Bhīma's command, nor learn of your return.
t.3.67.19: Whether he be prosperous, or whether he be without wealth, or whether he be desirous of riches, what he intends to do must be found out.
t.3.67.20: Thus addressed, O king, those brāhmaṇas then went forth in every direction to search for Nala, who had fallen into such misfortune.
t.3.67.21: Searching for Nala through cities together with their kingdoms, through villages, cattle-stations and hermitages, those brahmins, O king, did not find him.
t.3.67.22: And so, O lord of the people, all the Brahmins proclaimed that message here and there, just as it had been spoken by Damayantī.
